plans.name: 3 Day Gym Plan for Fat Loss
plans.subtitle: 3 full-body lifts + Zone 2 walks on your off days
plans.forWho: You can get to the gym 3 days a week and want to lose fat and keep muscle.
plans.promise: Lift 3 days, walk in Zone 2 on the others: build to 150 Zone 2 minutes a week in 6 weeks.
plans.whyItWorks: Lifting keeps or builds muscle. Zone 2 burns more fat for fuel than hard cardio, and it's easy to recover from, so the minutes add up week after week. Easy cardio doesn't blunt your lifting gains, and keeping Zone 2 on its own days keeps lift days short. Three full-body days work each muscle about three times a week.
cautions: Learn each lift with light weights first, and stop any lift that causes sharp pain.
Romanian deadlifts and walking lunges make legs sore in week 1. The Tuesday walk can be slower.
The Sunday walk is optional, not a catch-up for missed days.

plans.name: 5 Day Split + Zone 2
plans.subtitle: “I want to work out 5 days a week and burn fat”: here's the week
plans.forWho: You want to train 5 days a week: 3 lifts (glute focus), 2 Zone 2 days and a long weekend walk.
plans.promise: Train 5 days, burn more fat for fuel with real Zone 2 cardio, and close 150 Zone 2 minutes a week.
plans.whyItWorks: Lifting keeps or builds muscle, and easy cardio doesn't blunt those gains. Two dedicated Zone 2 days plus one long walk build steady minutes that are easy to recover from. Week 3 reaches 150 Zone 2 minutes, the amount health guidelines recommend, and week 4 is lighter on purpose so you come back fresh.
cautions: Thrusters and kettlebell swings are technical: learn them with light weights.
Hip thrusts and split squats can bother knees or hips. Swap in glute bridges or step-ups if they do.
The stair climber pushes most people out of Zone 2 fast, so use the slowest level only.
The bonus cardio after a lift is optional and never counted in the plan's minutes.

plans.name: Zone 2 Walking Starter
plans.subtitle: From zero to 150 Zone 2 minutes a week in 6 weeks
plans.forWho: New to exercise, or coming back after a break. No gym needed.
plans.promise: Go from zero to 150 Zone 2 minutes a week, the amount health guidelines recommend, just by walking.
plans.whyItWorks: It builds time first, the way exercise guidelines suggest for your first 4–6 weeks, and finishes at the 150 weekly minutes health guidelines recommend. Every bout counts, so even the 15-minute days matter. Brisk walking is the easiest way into Zone 2.
cautions: Very fit? Flat walking may not reach Zone 2. Add hills or an incline.
Less fit? Hills may push you into Zone 3. Slow down.
Chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness: stop and see a doctor.

plans.name: The Fat-Burning 12-3-30
plans.subtitle: The viral treadmill walk, tuned to your Zone 2
plans.forWho: You can walk 30 minutes, hate running, and want a treadmill routine.
plans.promise: The 12-3-30, made Zone 2: find the incline where your body burns more fat for fuel, and hold it.
plans.whyItWorks: Slow uphill walking is real cardio with less knee loading than fast flat walking, and walking burns more fat for fuel than cycling at the same effort. The classic 12% at 3 mph is a hard effort for most adults over 40, so this plan lets your heart rate set the incline and keeps you in Zone 2. It adds time first, with a lighter week 4. Week 6 is the test: can you do the real 12-3-30 and stay in Zone 2? If not, your own incline is the right one.
cautions: Raise the incline over weeks, not in one day: steep walking loads calves and Achilles tendons.
Don't hold the handrails. It hides the real effort.
Lower back or shin pain? Lower the incline.
Pregnant? Skip steep inclines and use the talk test.

plans.name: No-Treadmill Zone 2 Plan
plans.subtitle: Bike, elliptical, rower and more, easy on your joints
plans.forWho: You hate the treadmill (or running), or want low-impact cardio.
plans.promise: No treadmill, no running: hit your Zone 2 minutes on the machines you actually like.
plans.whyItWorks: Low-impact machines let you build Zone 2 minutes without pounding your joints. Your whole week of steady work, not the machine, is what drives fat loss, and every one of these machines counts toward your Zone 2 minutes. Heart rate runs lower on a bike, so adding resistance is the key. The talk test works on every machine.
cautions: Rowing with poor form strains the lower back: legs first, and keep it slow.
Rowers and stair climbers make it easy to drift above Zone 2.
Bike seat height matters for your knees: a slight bend at the bottom of each pedal stroke.

plans.name: Lift Heavy, Run Easy
plans.subtitle: 3 strength days + 3 Zone 2 cardio days: a hybrid week
plans.forWho: Lifters who want to run (or runners who want to lift). You can jog 20–30 min.
plans.promise: Get stronger and build your engine: 3 lifts and 150 Zone 2 minutes a week.
plans.whyItWorks: Easy cardio doesn't meaningfully reduce strength or muscle gains. Runs on their own days protect your lifting power, and the bike the day after leg day keeps cardio going with less impact. Keeping runs in Zone 2 makes them easy to recover from, which is the point of running easy. The minutes build to 150 over 5 weeks.
cautions: Zone 2 running is slow. Jogging very slowly, or walking, to stay in zone is normal.
Heavy squats and deadlifts need good technique. Get coaching if you're new to them.
Pain that changes how you move means rest. Running injuries are common in new runners.

plans.name: Walk to Easy Run
plans.subtitle: Start running the Zone 2 way: slow, easy, no gasping
plans.forWho: You walk comfortably and want to start running without hating it.
plans.promise: Go from walking to 35 minutes of easy running in 8 weeks, without gasping.
plans.whyItWorks: Run-walk builds are the standard way into running. Letting your heart rate decide when you jog keeps it in Zone 2, so it feels easy, and the talk test tells you the same. A lighter week 4 and no more than 3 runs a week keep the impact modest. The minutes shown are jog/walk minutes: walk breaks can dip below Zone 2, so your counted Zone 2 minutes may be a little lower.
cautions: Running is high-impact. Shin, knee or foot pain that lasts into the next day means repeat the week.
Very slow jogging, or walking, to stay in Zone 2 is normal at first.
Proper running shoes help.

plans.name: 150 to 300 Zone 2 Builder
plans.subtitle: Double your Zone 2 minutes in 8 weeks
plans.forWho: You already hit 150 a week and want the next level.
plans.promise: Build from 150 to 300 Zone 2 minutes a week, the top of the WHO's recommended range.
plans.whyItWorks: 300 minutes a week is the top of the WHO's recommended range, and more weekly minutes are linked with better fat-loss results in the research. Splitting some days into two walks makes the time fit a busy life, and every bout counts. Pair it with 2 strength sessions a week if you can, done before that day's Zone 2.
cautions: This is a lot of time on your feet. Swap in bike or elliptical days if feet, shins or knees complain.
Week 4 is lighter on purpose.
Eating less while you train? Watch your energy and sleep.
